descriptionChirho: Nifal feminine plural participle used substantivally for God's extraordinary acts of power and salvation — the most frequent usage of this root, referring to miraculous deeds in history, creation, and redemption (Arabic عَجَائِب ʿajāʾib, Korean 기이한 일들 gi-ihan ildeul, Swahili maajabu/miujiza).

Nifal stative/finite forms expressing that something is extraordinary, surpassing understanding or expectation — used of God's works, love, or knowledge that inspire awe (Arabic عَجِيبَة ʿajībah, Korean 기이하도다/놀라웠다, Swahili ajabu/vimenistaajabisha).

labelChirho: be too difficult, be beyond capacity
descriptionChirho: Nifal forms where the sense of being extraordinary extends to being beyond human ability or comprehension — 'too hard' or 'impossible' for someone, a well-attested semantic shift from wonder to difficulty (Arabic يَعْسُرُ/صَعُبَ yaʿsuru/ṣaʿuba 'be hard', Korean 너무 어렵다 neomu eoryeopda, Swahili ngumu sana/kushindikana).

Hifil causative forms expressing the act of performing extraordinary deeds or making something wonderful — God or an agent actively causes marvelous things to happen (Arabic أَعْجَبَ/أَظْهَرَ aʿjaba/aẓhara, Korean 기이하게 하다 gi-ihage hada, Swahili kufanya ajabu/maajabu).

Hifil forms in vow-specific contexts meaning to set apart or make special a votive offering — technical cultic usage where the extraordinary quality applies to a religious commitment (Arabic يَنْذِرُ/يُمَيِّزُ yanḏiru/yumayyizu, Korean 특별하게 하면/특별히 행하면, Swahili atafanya ajabu).

Piel intensive infinitive construct meaning to accomplish or carry out an extraordinary vow — the completion side of the vow process, distinct from the Hifil initiation (Arabic لِإِيفَاءِ/لِإِتْمَامِ li-īfāʾi/li-itmāmi 'for fulfillment', Korean 성취하기 위하여/이행하기 위하여, Swahili kutimiza).

Hitpael reflexive form expressing self-manifestation of extraordinary character — God reveals his own marvelous nature to someone (Arabic تَتَعَجَّبُ tataʿajjabu, Korean 기이한 일을 보이신다, Swahili unajionyesha wa ajabu).
